history.summary: The Shree Khatu Shyam Mandir on Shyam Mandir Marg, Samta Colony, Raipur, is dedicated to Khatu Shyam — Barbarika, son of Ghatotkacha and grandson of Bhima, who donated his head (sheesh-daan) to Krishna before the Kurukshetra war and was blessed to be worshipped in Krishna's name as Shyam in Kali Yuga. The temple enshrines a copy of the idol installed at the famous Khatu Shyam temple in Khatu village, Rajasthan. A grand annual event is held in the month of Phalgun. Coordinate is approximate (from a place listing, not the temple's own site).

name: Shree Khatu Shyam Mandir, Raipur
town_description: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh (since the state's formation in 2000) and its largest city, a major commercial and industrial hub of central India known for steel plants and rice milling. The old city around Purani Basti and the Kharun river preserves its pre-modern core, while newer areas like VIP Road and Naya Raipur reflect rapid recent growth. It is well connected by rail and air and serves as the gateway to Chhattisgarh's temples and national parks.
